Spotlight 2026 October                                                                                                               1

NATIONAL NEWS


          India Launches First PRAMAAN Forest Certificates

            What: Union Minister Bhupender Yadav handed over India's first PRAMAAN certificates under the
              Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme (IFWCS), marking the transition of the framework from
               policy to field-level implementation.

                Tell me more:

              The certificates were presented to the Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation (APFDC)
                    for plantations over 33,000 hectares, and to a bamboo farmer associated with the Odisha Bamboo
               Development Agency (OBDA).

            PRAMAAN helps Indian producers meet global regulatory requirements, including deforestation-
                  free timber sourcing norms adopted by major international markets.

                 Forest Management certification under PRAMAAN is based on the National Working Plan Code
             (NWPC) 2023, with certification bodies accredited by the National Accreditation Board for
                   Certification Bodies (NABCB).

              The scheme aims to create income opportunities for rural and tribal communities, smallholder
                 farmers, and forest-dependent communities, including Women Self-Help Groups.



         Cabinet Approves ₹1.86 Lakh Crore Green Corridor Scheme

            What: The Union Cabinet approved the ₹1.86 lakh crore Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme to
               build transmission infrastructure for evacuation of up to 135 GW of renewable power and deploy 50
         GWh of battery storage.

                Tell me more:

              The scheme, targeted for completion by FY 2032-33, allocates ₹1,36,378 crore for intra-state
                 transmission systems and ₹50,000 crore for Battery Energy Storage Systems.

              The Centre will provide financial assistance of ₹54,082 crore to offset intra-state transmission
                charges and limit the impact on electricity costs.

                   India is targeting 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, with the scheme contributing to a
                 longer-term target of 900 GW by 2035.

               Under the scheme, new transmission projects will be awarded through tariff-based competitive
                  bidding, while existing networks will be upgraded on a cost-plus basis.



       UPSC Begins Centenary Celebrations 'Manthan' in Delhi

            What: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) commenced its two-day centenary celebrations,
                 titled "Manthan", at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, marking 100 years since the institution's
             establishment on October 1, 1926.

                Tell me more:

            UPSC Chairman Dr. Ajay Kumar outlined the Commission's vision through three guiding principles:
                   Trust, Transparency, and Technology, while preserving core constitutional values.

              The Commission introduced AI-based facial authentication at scale for the Civil Services
                   (Preliminary) Examination on May 24, 2026, covering approximately 5.50 lakh candidates.





NATIONAL NEWS                                                                                                                  1

The constitutional framework governing Public Service Commissions is contained in Part XIV of
                 the Constitution, under Articles 315 to 323.



       CAG and BHASHINI Launch AI-Enabled Document Translation Solution

            What: Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) under Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of
              Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), in collaboration with Office of Comptroller and
              Auditor General of India (CAG), launched "CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad", an AI-enabled document
               translation solution for official CAG documents and audit-related reports.

                Tell me more:

                  Solution launched during closing ceremony of 74th Hindi Diwas (September 14) and Hindi
              Pakhwada 2026 (14 to 29 September) at CAG Office, New Delhi, attended by Comptroller and
                  Auditor General Shri K. Sanjay Murthy and senior CAG officials.

              CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad developed as customised Language AI solution focusing on consistent
                  terminology, contextual translation and quality of output, while addressing institutional
                 requirements for security, controlled access and data sovereignty.

              BHASHINI currently supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35
                   international languages, powering over 800 government websites with more than 9 billion
                 cumulative AI inferences and processing over 24 million AI inferences daily.



          Ministry of Education Approves Five Centres of Excellence For Classical Languages

            What: Ministry of Education approved Centres of Excellence (CoEs) for studies in five Classical
             languages (Assamese, Bengali, Marathi, Pali and Prakrit) to provide dedicated institutional support for
            advanced academic research, preservation and digitisation of linguistic and literary heritage.

                Tell me more:


                  Classical language  Centre of Excellence at                                     State

              Assamese         Tezpur University                                 Assam

                 Bengali             Visva-Bharati University                               West Bengal

                Marathi           Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, Pune  Maharashtra

                    Pali                 Central University of Odisha                             Odisha

                   Prakrit              Central University of Gujarat                                 Gujarat



         5th Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi

            What: The 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave conclave, organised by the Institute of Economic Growth
              (IEG) on the theme “Resilience in an Age of Flux”, in New Delhi, brought together policymakers,
             economists, academics, business leaders and other participants.

                Tell me more:

                IEG President N. K. Singh, IEG Board of Governors Chairman Michael Debabrata Patra and other
                   dignitaries were present on the occasion.

                  Shri Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog, highlighted need for regulatory frameworks to evolve
                 alongside rapidly changing geopolitical, technological and economic environment at 5th Kautilya
               Economic Conclave plenary session on "Regulatory Oversight in an Age of Disruption".





NATIONAL NEWS                                                                                                                  2

Gauba emphasised that India needs strict regulation for high-risk activities and simpler regulation
                    for low-risk activities to promote innovation, investment and economic growth towards Viksit
                 Bharat 2047.



          19th Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas Convention to be Held in Kolkata from January 7 to 9, 2027

            What: Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) announced that 19th edition of Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas (PBD)
             Convention will be held in Kolkata, West Bengal from January 7 to 9, 2027, organised by MEA in
              partnership with State Government of West Bengal.

                Tell me more:

                Convention aims to bring together members of Indian diaspora, young diaspora leaders,
                 entrepreneurs, professionals, academics, innovators and other stakeholders from across world.

                 President Droupadi Murmu will confer Pravasi Bharatiya Samman Awards. The event will also
                  feature Youth Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas (PBD) Convention providing platform for young members of
                  Indian diaspora.

                 Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas celebrated on January 9 every year to mark contribution of overseas
                  Indian community to development of India; date commemorates return of Mahatma Gandhi to India
                from South Africa on January 9, 1915.

                Since 2015, the format of PBD has been revised with the convention being held once every two
                 years and theme-based PBD Conferences being organised during the intervening period.

              The 18th PBD Convention was held from January 8 to 10, 2025 in Bhubaneswar, Odisha with
               theme "Diaspora's Contribution to a Viksit Bharat". Christine Carla Kangaloo, President of the
                 Republic of Trinidad and Tobago, was the Chief Guest in PBD 2025.



          India Japan Launch JCM Operational Manual

            What: India and Japan launched the Operational Manual for the Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM),
              establishing procedures to implement bilateral cooperation on low-carbon technologies, climate
              finance and emission reductions.

                Tell me more:

              The JCM will promote advanced low-carbon technologies, technology cooperation and climate
                 finance while supporting emission reductions and removals in India.

              The mechanism operates under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement, following the Memorandum of
                Cooperation signed in August 2025 and Rule of Implementation adopted in June 2026.

              The Manual provides a clear framework covering the complete project cycle, from submitting a
                  Project Idea Note to issuing and authorizing JCM credits.

              The mechanism aims to support sustainable development and strengthen transparency and
                confidence in international carbon markets.



         10th Edition of India Mobile Congress 2026 Held in New Delhi

            What: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress
             (IMC) at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi under the theme of “Scale Without Boundaries”.

                Tell me more:

              The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI)
                     jointly organised IMC 2026 from October 7 to 10.





NATIONAL NEWS                                                                                                                  3

The event features the Ministerial Programme on “Investing in the Next Billion Digital Connections”,
            CEO Roundtable on “The Sovereign Inflection & the Future of Telecom”, AI for Good, and Cyber
                  Security Summit.

              The programme also included the 6G Symposium, Startup World Cup India 2026, ITU Build-A-
              Thon on AI Agents for 5G Networks, AI Safety India-UK Panel, and Robotics for Youth Challenge.

                Union Minister Jyotiraditya M. Scindia participated in the CEO Round Table on The Sovereign
                    Inflection & The Future of Telecom and highlighted India’s position as the world’s second-largest
                telecom market and second-largest mobile phone producer.

                 Scindia also inaugurated Workshop on 5G Use Case Labs held under theme "Building Intelligent
                Networks: Innovations Driving the 5G Advanced and 6G Era".

               100 5G Use Case Labs established in October 2023 with outlay of ₹97.67 crore became
                  operational by April 2025, delivering 634 products and use cases with 158 intellectual property
                     filings and 32 patents granted by August 2026.

              The 5G Innovation Hackathon (Edition-2) 2026 invited technology-based solutions across
               emerging telecommunications fields and received over 1,400 proposals.

               Of these, 50 teams received seed funding to develop their ideas, while 35 showcased their
                 innovations at India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026.

                 Robotics for Good Youth Challenge India 2026-2027:

                       International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and DoT organised Robotics for Good Youth
                    Challenge India 2026-2027, bringing together 57 teams with around 300 students and mentors
                   from 14 States, designing solutions for UN SDG 3 on good health and well-being.

                 The challenge is part of the ITU’s AI for Good programme, featuring 28 Junior and 29 Senior
                   Category teams.

                 Teams competed in two categories

                        Senior Category Winner: Team Ferrum Incubators from Cambridge School, Noida, Uttar
                       Pradesh.

                         Junior Category Winner: Team Singularity from Gopalan International School, Karnataka.

                   Both winning teams will represent India at the Grand Finale in Geneva, Switzerland, during the
                      AI for Good Global Summit in June 2027.

                 The challenge began in 2024 during the World Telecommunication Standardization Assembly
                   (WTSA-24), hosted by India, and continued at India Mobile Congress (IMC) in 2025 and 2026.



         Cabinet Approves ₹10,000 Crore SME Growth Fund and Integrated Transport Logistics Authority

            What: Union Cabinet approved ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund to provide direct equity investments in
              small and medium enterprises, and setting up of Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) for
              greater coordination and multimodal integration across transport ecosystem.

                Tell me more:

               Government will provide ₹10,000 crore to an Alternative Investment Fund under the SME Growth
               Fund framework announced in Union Budget 2026-27 to mobilise capital for manufacturing,
                  services, innovation-driven sectors and strategic value chains

            SME Growth Fund will help enterprises scale, adopt advanced technologies, expand
                 manufacturing, enter global markets and join global value chains through equity, liquidity and
                  professional support.





NATIONAL NEWS                                                                                                                  4

Cabinet also approved a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) as the Integrated Transport and Logistics
                  Authority (ITLA).

                ITLA will serve as the national apex institution for integrated transport and logistics projects. Its
                  functions will include research, project appraisal, policy support, monitoring and data analytics,
                addressing fragmented planning across transport Ministries and agencies.



         Health Ministry Launches JOSH Teams to Strengthen Youth Participation in TB

            What: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare will launch Joint Squad for Health (JOSH) Teams in
          New Delhi to involve young people in tuberculosis (TB) awareness, prevention and community
            engagement.

                Tell me more:

              The first phase will cover 55 districts across 11 States, focusing on youth-led community
                  mobilisation for the TB Mukt Bharat campaign.

             JOSH Teams will strengthen Block and community-level engagement by spreading information on
             TB symptoms, prevention, timely diagnosis and completion of treatment among local communities.

              The launch will involve the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Ministry of Youth Affairs and
                  Sports, MY Bharat Volunteers, National Cadet Corps (NCC) Cadets and other stakeholders.



          Third Edition of Sagarmanthan Dialogue Begins in Delhi

            What: The third edition of Sagarmanthan: The Great Oceans Dialogue will bring together more than
             1,200 participants from nearly 75 countries in New Delhi from October 7 to 9 to discuss the future of
              the global maritime sector.

                Tell me more:

              The dialogue is co-hosted by the Observer Research Foundation (ORF) and the Ministry of Ports,
                 Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), under the theme "Blue Geographies, New Aspirations: Trade,
                Technology, and Trust at Sea".

               Launched in New Delhi in 2024 and held in Mumbai in 2025, Sagarmanthan is an annual platform
                    for policymakers, industry leaders, and scholars to discuss the blue economy, ports, and shipping.

              The conference centres on five pillars, including "Steady Straits", "Blue Breakthroughs: Greening
                Ships and Shipbuilding", and "Ocean Societies: Communities, Cultures, and Livelihoods".

              The dialogue aligns with India's Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047, which places ports, shipping, and
                 the blue economy at the centre of the country's long-term growth.

             DP World is the logistics partner, along with Konrad Adenauer Stiftung, the Korea Institute for
                   International Economic Policy, and Fincantieri.

              The governments of the Netherlands and Norway are also partners, with the Organisation for
               Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), German Maritime Museum, and MENA2050 as
               knowledge partners.



          India Joins 14 Economies Against Excess Capacity

            What: India joined the United States (US) and 13 other economies in calling for measures to reduce
            excess production and end policies that distort global markets.

                Tell me more:





NATIONAL NEWS                                                                                                                  5

The Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) released the statement after G20 Trade
                   Ministers’ discussions held in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on September 30 and October 1, 2026.

              The 15 signatories include Argentina, Australia, Canada, the European Union, France, Germany,
                    India, Italy, Japan, the Republic of Korea, Mexico, Poland, Türkiye, the United Kingdom and the US.

              The initial sectors include automobiles, electric vehicles, batteries, chemicals, foundational
                semiconductors and solar panels, with sector-specific platforms planned to develop rules and
                share excess-production data.



        MoSPI Releases Strategy for Environmental-Economic Accounts in India 2026 to 2030

            What: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) released 'Strategy for
             Environmental-Economic Accounts in India 2026-2030' building on earlier 2022-26 roadmap to
             strengthen environmental accounting covering forests, minerals, soil resources, land, water, carbon
              stock, biodiversity and environment-related activities.

                Tell me more:

              The strategy document identifies data gaps, suggests data sources and provides an action plan to
                develop environmental-economic accounts. It also helps States and Union Territories improve
                 environmental accounting systems.

              The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has followed the System of
                Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) since 2018. The earlier 2022–26 strategy covered
                  Material Flow Accounts, Ocean Accounts, Energy Accounts and biodiversity and urban accounts.

              The document provides a framework for developing environmental-economic accounting in India
                 during 2026–30. It selects focus areas based on the GreenNationalAccountinIndia: AFramework
                  report and SEEA-CF.

              The document reviews India’s progress in environmental accounting and outlines MoSPI’s steps to
                address data gaps, improve accounting and guide work during the coming years.



        Government Reconstitutes Press Council of India with 13 Members

            What: Government reconstituted Press Council of India (PCI) on October 8, 2026, by nominating 13
            members, including six editors and seven working journalists, under provisions of Press Council Act,
              1978.

                Tell me more:

                PCI is headed by Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai (retd).

                PCI is a statutory autonomous body established under Press Council Act, 1978, mainly to preserve
                press freedom and improve standards of newspapers and news agencies in India.



       Commerce Department Creates FTA Cell To Boost Export Opportunities

            What: Department of Commerce established Free Trade Agreement (FTA) Utilisation Cell to help
             domestic businesses understand agreements, identify opportunities in partner markets and increase
            use of FTAs through industry associations, Export Promotion Councils and State Governments.

                Tell me more:

                   Cell will explain FTA benefits, prepare market-specific action plans with Export Promotion Councils
               and support implementation over the next four to five years.





NATIONAL NEWS                                                                                                                  6

Department will conduct discussions with States, industry and exporters during October, followed
               by district-level workshops during the current financial year.

                   India has finalised trade pacts with European Free Trade Association (EFTA), New Zealand,
                  Mauritius, United Arab Emirates, Australia, Oman, European Union and United Kingdom.

                EFTA, European Union and United Kingdom agreements together cover 32 countries, with majority
                  of India's trade expected at zero tariffs; agreements provide tariff predictability, supporting
                 investment risks, supply-chain planning and business growth.

              EFTA accounts for less than 1% of India's total imports, valued at about USD 2-3 billion;
             Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal suggested increasing India's share to 2% of EFTA's import
                basket within three to four years.



          Liechtenstein’s Hereditary Prince Alois on First State Visit to India

            What: Hereditary Prince Alois, Acting Head of State of Liechtenstein, made his first State visit to India,
            marking the first anniversary of the India–European Free Trade Association (EFTA) Trade and
            Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA).

                Tell me more:

                India–EFTA TEPA: It was signed in March 2024 and came into force in October 2025. It aims to
                  bring $100 billion of investment into India and create one million direct jobs in India over 15 years.

               Key outcomes:


                   Area                                 Outcome

                                                                    Liechtenstein will support India’s bid for UNSC non-
              UNSC                                   permanent membership (2028-29); both agreed on UN reform
                                                               through initiatives like UN80.

                   Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement
                                                                         India received Liechtenstein’s draft DTAA for consideration.
                  (DTAA)

                                                             Both sides agreed that AI governance should be grounded in
                      AI governance
                                                                          international law, including human rights law.

              2nd India–EFTA Prosperity Summit in New Delhi: Tata Power signed an agreement with Norway-
               based Ocean Sun at the summit to bring membrane-based floating solar technology to India.



        Windergy India 2026 Showcases India’s Growing Wind Energy Sector

            What: Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi inaugurated the 8th edition of
            Windergy India 2026 at Chennai Trade Centre, focusing on manufacturing, technology and investment
                in wind energy.

                Tell me more:

                   India added record 6.05 gigawatts of wind power capacity during financial year 2025-26, taking
                 cumulative installed capacity to 58.52 gigawatts by August 2026.

                Another 28 gigawatts remains under implementation, supporting India’s target of achieving 100
                 gigawatts of wind power capacity by 2030.

               Around 400 exhibitors from over 20 countries and 500 delegates will participate, with country
                   pavilions from Denmark, Germany and Spain.



          India and Estonia Explore Wider Technology and Trade Cooperation





NATIONAL NEWS                                                                                                                  7

What: India and Estonia are exploring broader cooperation in technology, clean energy, defence,
             education and research, with Estonia’s Ambassador Kristi Karelsohn highlighting opportunities to
            expand bilateral trade, investment and business ties.

                Tell me more:

                    Bilateral trade reached approximately €200 million in 2025. Estonia sees opportunities in artificial
                   intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, industrial digitalisation, clean energy and specialised defence
                  technologies.



        Supreme Court Constitutes Standing Committee on Judicial Well-being

            What: Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant constituted a Standing Committee on Judicial Well-
             being under the Supreme Court of India on World Mental Health Day (October 10, 2026), chaired by
              Justice K.V. Viswanathan, to address professional and personal well-being of judicial officers.

                Tell me more:

               Committee follows research by Centre for Research and Planning, Supreme Court of India,
                examining occupational stress, workload, exhaustion, staffing shortages, infrastructure limitations,
                   transfers, work-life balance and institutional support.

              The initiative is based on the Nauru Declaration on Judicial Well-being, adopted on July 25, 2024.

                  Further reinforcing this global commitment, the United Nations General Assembly, in March 2025,
                proclaimed 25 July of every year as the International Day for Judicial Well-being.

           Knowledge Nuggets:

              The 2026 International Judicial Conference on Integrity and Judicial Well-being will be held in
               Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands, from 4 to 6 November 2026.

              The Conference is organised by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime in collaboration
                 with the Cayman Islands Judiciary and the Secretariat for Judicial Well-being in Papua New
                 Guinea.

             Theme of International Day for Judicial Well-being 2026: “Judicial Well-being and Integrity: From
                   Individual Resilience to Institutional Responsibility.”



        Supreme Court Reviews 10 Years of Juvenile Justice Act Implementation

            What: The Supreme Court held a two-day national consultation to review the implementation of the
              Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, and identify priorities for improving child
              protection and juvenile justice.

                Tell me more:

              The consultation was organised by the Supreme Court’s Juvenile Justice Committee in
                  collaboration with UNICEF India.



        Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat Trains

            What: Indian Railways operates Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat trains to serve different passenger
             needs, offering premium air-conditioned travel through Vande Bharat and affordable non-air-
             conditioned travel through Amrit Bharat.

                Tell me more:





NATIONAL NEWS                                                                                                                  8

As of July 2026, Indian Railways operated 162 Vande Bharat Chair Car services, two Vande Bharat
                 Sleeper services and 72 Amrit Bharat services.

              Vande Bharat offers air-conditioned Chair Car, Executive Chair Car and Sleeper accommodation.
              Vande Bharat has a design speed of 180 kmph and an operating speed of up to 160 kmph,
               depending on route conditions.

                 Amrit Bharat is fully non-air-conditioned, with 11 General Class coaches, eight Sleeper Class
                coaches, one Pantry Car and two Luggage-cum-Divyangjan coaches. It aims to provide faster
                 journeys than conventional trains but lacks the same operating-speed specification as Vande
                  Bharat.

              As of March 2026, a total of 60 Amrit Bharat Express services are being operated on the Indian
                 Railways network, as per the official PIB release.



           Textile Minister Projections for Textile Industry

            What: Union Textile Minister Giriraj Singh stated India's textile industry expanded to nearly $190 billion
                in 2025-26, poised to achieve target of $350 billion by 2030, with domestic market growing from
             about ₹6 lakh crore in 2014-15 to over ₹16 lakh crore.

                Tell me more:

                   Textile and apparel sector is expected to generate nearly 2 crore additional jobs over next three
                 years under Prime Minister's 5F vision connecting Farm to Fibre, Fibre to Factory, Factory to
                Fashion and Fashion to Foreign.

               Government implemented landmark reforms including PM MITRA Parks, PLI Scheme, National
                 Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM), Textiles Export Promotion Mission (TEEM), National Fibre
                 Mission and Raw Material Support Scheme (RMSS) for textile sector.

                   India's network of Free Trade Agreements expanded from 10 FTAs covering 19 countries in 2014 to
                 18 FTAs covering 56 countries, with technical textiles market expanding from about $6 billion to
              $25 billion under NTTM.



          India and Qatar Review Strategic Partnership at 6th FOC

            What: India and Qatar reviewed their strategic partnership during the 6th India-Qatar Foreign Office
              Consultations (FOC) in New Delhi, discussing cooperation across key sectors and regional
             developments, including West Asia.

                Tell me more:

                   Sripriya Ranganathan, Secretary in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), and Ahmad Hassen Al-
              Hammadi, Secretary General of Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, co-chaired the consultations.

                Both countries discussed cooperation in trade, investment, energy, security, education, culture
               and political affairs, along with regional and global issues, particularly developments in West Asia.

                Both countries agreed to hold the next round of consultations in Doha on a mutually convenient
                  date.



       NHRC Marks 33rd Foundation Day with Water Conference

            What: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) celebrated its 33rd Foundation Day at Vigyan
            Bhawan, New Delhi. NHRC was set up on October 12, 1993.

                Tell me more:





NATIONAL NEWS                                                                                                                  9

Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant attended as the Chief Guest, while NHRC Chairperson
                  Justice V Ramasubramanian addressed the function.

            NHRC held a National Conference on the theme ‘Water as the Elixir of Life: Advancing Human
                  Dignity through the Right to Water’.

            NHRC also launched the NHRC, India mobile application and moved towards digitising its records
                   to make the Commission more accessible.



         MeitY Selects CoRover.ai for Government Agentic AI Platform

            What: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has selected CoRover.ai to
               build a unified agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) platform for government services, with DigiLocker as
                   its first implementation.

                Tell me more:

              The National e-Governance Division (NeGD) awarded the contract through a quality-and-cost
               based selection, where CoRover scored 100 against 91.24 for Kyndryl Solutions.

              The common platform will enable government departments to build and manage AI assistants and
                 bots for various services, including DigiLocker document-related tasks.

                            It will provide tools to develop and manage AI agents, safeguard against prompt injection and
                    jailbreak attempts, and ensure agents access connected government systems only after
                  authentication and user consent.

           Knowledge Nuggets:

                  Jailbreaking in computer and mobile security is the act of removing software or hardware
                    restrictions imposed by a manufacturer, allowing users to gain root-level or administrative
                 permissions.



        EAM’s Three-Nation Africa Tour

            What: External Affairs Minister (EAM) S. Jaishankar visited Ghana, Côte d’Ivoire and Ethiopia.

                Tell me more:

               Ghana: Jaishankar met Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama in Accra. India and Ghana have
               a Comprehensive Partnership.

                India–Ghana MoUs:

                     Zoological Survey of India and University of Ghana, on academic research and capacity
                       building.

                      Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and Ghana’s CSIR-Crops Research Institute, on
                       agricultural research and education.

                   International Big Cat Alliance: Ghana handed over its Instrument of Acceptance to join the alliance.

               Côte d’Ivoire: India–Côte d’Ivoire bilateral trade is over US$1.5 billion.

                   Ethiopia: India will hold the next Jaipur Artificial Limb Fitment Camp in Ethiopia. The 2024 camp in
                 the Afar region helped about 450 beneficiaries.

                 The EAM chaired the Regional Heads of Mission Conference in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.



         3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium Held in Delhi





NATIONAL NEWS                                                                                                                 10

What: Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya M. Scindia inaugurated the 3rd International Bharat
          6G Symposium 2026, organised by the Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) from 7–9 October at Yashobhoomi,
            Dwarka, New Delhi.

                Tell me more:

             B6GA exchanged five new Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with GSMA, one6G Association,
                GTI Alliance Ltd, 6G Industry Forum (6GIF) and VoICE.

             B6GA already had 10 global and 2 domestic collaborations, and the new MoUs take its total
                 partnership network to 17.

             B6GA also released nine Working Group white papers on topics such as spectrum readiness,
                sensing and communication, optical technologies, sustainability and security.

            A joint report released at the event tracks one year of progress towards the 6G principles of the
            New Delhi Declaration, endorsed at the 2025 symposium.

              The New Delhi Declaration provides a common framework for a secure, open, inclusive and
                  sustainable 6G ecosystem through international cooperation in research and standards.



        IGNCA Hosts Conference on India’s Global Cultural Connections

            What: The Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) is hosting the ‘Brihattar Bharat:
               International Conference on Bharat’s Cultural Connections Across the Globe’ at Vigyan Bhawan from
            October 14-16.

                Tell me more:

              IGNCA works under the Ministry of Culture, and the conference focuses on India’s cultural legacy
               and civilisational heritage beyond its borders.

              The conference marks the centenary of the Greater India Society (Brihattar Bharat Parishad), set
              up in Calcutta on October 14, 1926, with Rabindranath Tagore as its spiritual guide.



          India-France TRISHNA Satellite Targets Water and Crop Monitoring

            What: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) plans to launch the India-France Thermal Infra-
           Red Imaging Satellite for High-resolution Natural Resource Assessment (TRISHNA) mission by 2027 or
              early 2028 to monitor water stress, crop health and urban heat.

                Tell me more:

              TRISHNA will provide Earth observation data at nearly 60-metre resolution and revisit the same
                  location every three days near the equator.

              The satellite will carry two instruments: a thermal infrared instrument developed by Airbus
               Defence and Space under France’s Centre National d’Études Spatiales (CNES), and another
                 instrument developed by ISRO.

              The mission will monitor evapotranspiration, vegetation, water quality, urban heat islands, glacier
               dynamics and surface temperatures to support water and food security research.

              The satellite will operate in a sun-synchronous orbit approximately 761 km above Earth, with a
                planned mission life of five years.



          21st MSDC Adopts Maritime Vision Targets in Mumbai





NATIONAL NEWS                                                                                                                 11

                 Bengal, addressing terrorism, trafficking, cybercrime, smuggling and piracy, condemning cross-
                border terrorism and urging implementation of UN Security Council sanctions.

              BIMSTEC members will follow global anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing
                 standards, strengthen partnerships with Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG), UNODC,
              INTERPOL and FATF, and implement action plans on money laundering, human trafficking and
                  narcotic drugs.

                  Crime and Illicit Drug Trafficking has been in force since March 2021.

                 The BIMSTEC Convention on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters was signed in March
                 2022 at the 5th Summit in Colombo.

                   Conventions on Extradition, Transfer of Sentenced Persons and Trafficking in Persons still
                     await finalisation.

             Members discussed the need to develop a BIMSTEC Drug Offences Monitoring Desk (BDOMD)
               and also proposed a Regional Information-Sharing Mechanism on Trafficking in Persons and
               Smuggling of Migrants.

                  National Security Chiefs have started a Track 1.5 BIMSTEC Security Dialogue and an initiative for a
                Himalayan Science Council.

           Knowledge Nuggets:

              BIMSTEC is a regional organisation of seven countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar,
                 Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.

              The Bangkok Declaration established the grouping on June 6, 1997, initially as Bangladesh-India-
                    Sri Lanka-Thailand Economic Cooperation (BIST-EC).

              Myanmar joined on December 22, 1997, while Nepal and Bhutan joined in 2004.

              BIMSTEC cooperation covers agriculture and food security, blue economy, connectivity, culture,
                  disaster management, energy, environment and climate change, fiscal and monetary policy,
                   health, human resource development, fisheries and livestock, and people-to-people relations.

STATE NEWS                                                                                                                     11

Presidential assent: President Droupadi Murmu

               Passed unanimously by: Nagaland Legislative Assembly

               Based on: Article 371A of the Constitution

                Background:

                    Since 2010, the Eastern Nagaland People’s Organisation (ENPO), representing the tribes of the
                        six eastern districts, has demanded a separate state, saying the region lags behind in
                   development.

                 As a compromise, the Centre, the Nagaland government and ENPO agreed to self-rule within
                    Nagaland, which led to the FNTA.

                 The FNTA is an autonomous authority within Nagaland, not a separate state, with powers to
                make laws, run administration and handle finances for the six eastern districts.

                            Its members will be elected. Until then, an interim council set up by the state government will
                    run its affairs for up to one year.

               ENPO tribes (8): Chang, Khiamniungan, Konyak, Phom, Sangtam, Tikhir, Yimkhiung and
                    Eastern Sumi

                    Article 371A:

               A special provision for Nagaland, added by the 13th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1962.
                  Under it, no Act of Parliament on Naga religious or social practices, Naga customary law, or
                   ownership and transfer of land and its resources applies to Nagaland unless the Nagaland
                       Legislative Assembly approves it by a resolution.
